title: How a single fixed pulley helps you lift
examples: Does a single pulley make lifting easier?
Why does a flagpole have a pulley?
How does a pulley at the top of a well help?

explain.say: A fixed pulley is a grooved wheel hung from a hook, with a rope over it. One end of the rope holds the load, and you pull the other end.

draw.text: How a single fixed pulley helps you lift

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: pulleys. Look at the fixed pulley, the movable pulley and the rope. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: How a single fixed pulley helps you lift

explain.say: You pull down, and the rope carries that pull over the wheel so the load goes up. Pulling down is easier than lifting up, because you can use your body weight.
But to lift a 100 newton load you still pull with about 100 newtons, a little more because of friction. A single fixed pulley changes the direction of the force, not its size.
Look at the hook: both rope ends pull down on the pulley, so the hook must hold up twice the load. Flagpoles, window blinds and wells all use fixed pulleys to lift from below.

faq.q: Does a single pulley make lifting easier?
faq.a: A single fixed pulley does not reduce the force: you pull with about the same force as the load's weight. It makes lifting easier by letting you pull down, with your weight helping, instead of lifting up.
asks: Does one pulley halve the weight?

faq.q: Why do I pull down to lift the load up?
faq.a: The rope runs over the wheel, so it turns your downward pull into an upward pull on the load. The pulley changes the direction of the force.
asks: How does a pulley change direction?

faq.q: How heavy does the load feel with one pulley?
faq.a: About the same as its weight, plus a little extra to overcome friction in the wheel.
asks: Is it lighter with a pulley?

faq.q: Why must the hook be strong?
faq.a: Both ends of the rope pull down on the pulley, one with the load's weight and one with your pull. So the hook holds about twice the load.
asks: How much force is on the pulley hook?

faq.q: How do you make a pulley that reduces the force?
faq.a: Use a movable pulley attached to the load, or a block and tackle with several wheels. The load then hangs on two or more rope strands, which share it.

facts: A single fixed pulley has a mechanical advantage of 1: it only changes the direction of the force.
The support of a single fixed pulley carries about twice the load's weight.

quiz.say: With one fixed pulley, how hard must you pull to lift a 200 N load?
quiz.show: With one fixed pulley, how hard must you pull to lift a 200 N load?
quiz.why: A single fixed pulley does not reduce the force, so you need about 200 N, a little more for friction.

wrong.0: Halving the force needs a movable pulley with two rope strands.
wrong.2: The hook feels about 400 N, but you only pull about 200 N.
